test.name: Single record already in hand should route to record-extraction, not start a search
test.description: The user has already captured an individual record page and wants its contents extracted into the research files. That is record-extraction's job — search-external-sites' capture-analysis step is the triage of a results LIST, and even that hands selected records to record-extraction. The skill's description carves this out ('Do NOT use when the user wants to analyze a single record already in context').

input.user_message: I've saved the individual record page for Patrick Flynn from the Ancestry search as a PDF — extract the names, dates, and places from it into the research files.

negative.explanation: A single captured record page going into the research files is assertion extraction — record-extraction's purpose. search-external-sites generates search URLs and triages results lists; its own workflow explicitly passes individual selected records to record-extraction. Re-firing search-external-sites here would either re-search (wrong) or duplicate record-extraction's extraction logic (also wrong).

judge_context: This is a grade_on_invariant negative test: PASS/FAIL is decided solely by the deterministic no-search-no-write validator (no external_links_search call, no new external_site log entry). Routing and activation are NOT gated. The judge runs base-only and diagnostically here — its scores do not decide the outcome.

Ideal behavior is to hand the already-captured single record to record-extraction (via a Skill('record-extraction') call or a one-line hand-off) rather than generating a new search URL or re-triaging the record itself. Note in your rationale whether the skill routed cleanly.

Known model prior (why this was previously flaky, issue #1519): the model's decline is correct nearly every run, but its phrasing varies — a decline that engages with the request ("upload the PDF and I'll hand it to record-extraction") was read by the activation heuristic as substantive output and failed the test, while a terser hand-off passed. Every deterministic input was identical across the passing and failing runs. Under grade_on_invariant the decline phrasing no longer decides the outcome; only executing or logging an external-site search does.

record-extraction holds research_log_append and may legitimately write a non-external_site log entry for the record it was handed. That is the correct skill doing its own job, not harm, and the validator is scoped to external_site entries for exactly that reason.
